evidence.claim: Our exp51 port on 4 videos (143,634 peaks) shows how far the public V1284 head really moves peaks: mean 0.74 um (0.71-0.84 per video), max 1.61 um, and only 10.5% of peaks move by 1 um or more. It never reaches its 2 um cap. That is the size of the peak-grid quantisation error (1.625 um grid, RMS 0.81 um in 3D). So the head removes quantisation; it does not correct 5-10 um offsets.
evidence.source: scratchpad out_exp51/coordhead_stats_{0,1}_2.jsonl and biohub-exp51-coordhead.log (COORDHEAD SUMMARY line)

evidence.claim: The head file keeps only state_dict, mean and scale. The MLP is 224->32->3 over 32 channels x 7 stencil points, with a norm-bounded output of 2*d/(1+|d|) that stays under 2 um. On synthetic N(0,1) inputs the shift is 0.40 um at q50 and 0.86 um at q99.

Arithmetic check: removing only the quantisation error should cut the median centre distance from 1.72 to about 1.52 um, i.e. -11.7%. x138 reports -10.4% held out. So the '10% shrink = x138 +0.007' consistency argument in the hypothesis matches in size only; the head does not shrink tail offsets in the direction of GT.

Direct learnability test: can a learned model predict the peak-to-GT offset from local image content? Setup: 24 tail-rich 6bba videos, 7,019 GT nodes with the nearest peak under 10 um (798 of them at 7-10 um). Input: a 13^3 raw-image patch of about +-10 um around the peak, which is wider context than a 3x3x3 or 5x5x5 feature stencil. Validation: GroupKFold by video. Result: the correlation between prediction and target on the tail is |r| <= 0.09 on every axis. Ridge moves the >=7 um count from 798 to 755 (106 rescued, 63 pushed out) and grows the 4-7 um zone from 1,021 to 1,119. HGB with L1 loss gives 760 (97/59) and a 4-7 um zone of 1,042. A 3 um z / 2 um xy cap changes nothing.
evidence.source: scratchpad headlearn.py (run 24 Sep, CPU 2 min); notes file

evidence.claim: In-sample argument: the detector heatmap was trained with single-voxel targets at these same GT points on all 199 videos. It still places a confident peak (p ~ 1.0) 7-10 um away on the same bright object, with no intensity valley in 96% of cases. The tail is therefore what the network could not fit (off-centre clicks or annotator noise). A head reading the same frozen features has no extra information about it.
evidence.source: r1_hyp_detection.notes.md (valley test, miss geometry); train_unet_transformer.py target construction (polyphase notes)

evidence.claim: Offsets are heterogeneous per node. Removing the embryo or per-video mean offset does not help (0.9831-0.9835 vs 0.9843 within 7 um), and a constant shift lost 0.0031 on the LB. About half of the offset variance is frame-level noise (lag-1 autocorrelation z 0.57, lag-5 0.31), which a per-frame head cannot predict.
evidence.source: r1_hyp_detection.notes.md (bias oracle, autocorr.py); CONTEXT forum note (Le Quang Canh / zhincez)

evidence.claim: The host describes GT nodes as 'approximate cell centers'. The landmark literature finds inter-rater error about 1.8x intra-rater error, and models observer variability with anisotropic Gaussians. Both are consistent with an irreducible, mostly axial annotation spread.
Quantisation-offset regression and training-free sub-pixel decoding recover only the grid error. This is the ceiling of what the head family can do from peak-centred features.
evidence.source: DARK, Zhang et al. CVPR 2020 (arXiv 1910.06278); CenterNet/CenterPoint offset heads

implementation_notes: Our code and data facts. (a) The x138 head takes 224-d input = 32 UNet channels x 7 points (centre plus 6 face neighbours on the 1.625 um grid), z-scored with the stored mean and scale. The output is a norm-bounded shift 2*d/(1+|d|) in um. The patch is applied after peak extraction and before coord_offset, and the edge transformer gathers features trilinearly at the float coordinates. (b) PITFALL: exp39's write_test_submission and the lab replay (replay.py) both round z, y and x to integers, so any z refinement under 0.81 um is lost at output. The float-output-coords idea measured +0.0017 from floats alone on the lab tail (CI90 [+0.0008, +0.0025]), so a head gain must be measured with float output ON in both arms. Write every coordinate with a decimal point, because polars schema inference types a column from its first rows. (c) The gate-aware softplus loss and a 3 um z cap buy nothing, because the tail target is not predictable (|r| <= 0.09). A wider cap only adds crossed-out nodes: ridge pushes out 63 nodes for 106 rescued, a net gain of 43 of 798 (5%), roughly what a mean shift gives. (d) Track-identity pairing out to 10 um adds noisy targets (the annotation noise itself) and dilutes the de-quantisation signal. Guess: it would make the head worse at the <4 um job it actually does. (e) Transfer: 6bba mean dz -0.85 um vs 44b6 -0.17 um. Any head that learns a bias learns the train-embryo convention, the same failure mode as zhincez's -0.0031. (f) What remains is the idea already listed as #2 in browser_research_2026-09-24: retrain the same small head on the 199-video capture with plain Huber loss, a 2 um cap and GroupKFold by leak group, i.e. a better de-quantiser. The 4-movie head was 14.9% worse than the 20-movie one, so data volume matters up to 20 movies. Whether 20 -> 199 movies still helps is unknown (guess: small, saturating). (g) Detector peaks are in-sample on train, so train peaks sit closer to GT than on test. A head trained on train pairs learns an under-sized correction (a safe direction).
refined_change: Drop the gate-aware and tail-recovery parts: the 7-10 um tail is annotation spread that neither image nor features predict, so do not widen the cap, change the loss or pair by track identity. The only defensible residual is a plain retrain of the V1284-architecture head (32 ch x 7-point stencil, plus an optional 27-point 3x3x3 variant) on a 199-video capture: Huber loss on GT-minus-peak for pairs under 4 um only, the 2 um norm-bounded output, GroupKFold over 44b6 leak groups and 6bba videos, with the final head trained on all videos. Ship it only if its OOF de-quantisation beats the public head. Always pair it with float output coordinates. For the ~2,700 swap and tail FN, spend the effort on duplicate or track-level position handling (e.g. refined duplicate collapse, track-context pooling), not on per-peak regression.
refined_lab_test: Step 0 (done, CPU): image-patch learnability, null on the tail (see evidence). Step 1 (Kaggle GPU, about 0.5-1 h, kill test): V1284_MODE=capture on 24 tail-rich 6bba videos plus 12 44b6 videos (one per leak group), dumping 32-ch features on 7-point and 27-point stencils for every raw peak within 12 um of a GT node. On Kaggle CPU, train OOF heads (GroupKFold by video/leak group): (i) plain Huber on pairs under 4 um, (ii) the proposed gate-aware loss with the 3z/2xy cap. Compare them with the public head applied to the same features. Report per embryo: share <4 um (base about 0.925 globally), 4-7 um count, >=7 um count, and tail rescued vs crossed out. KILL the gate-aware variant if its net tail rescue (rescued minus crossed out) is under 15% of tail nodes or its 4-7 um zone is not at least 5% below the public head's. KILL the plain retrain if its <4 um share is not at least +0.005 above the public head on both embryos. Step 2, only if a variant survives: capture on all 199 videos (3-5 GPU h), then the Step B replay with float output ON in both arms (exp48+ef+port+float vs the same plus the new head), SELECTION -> CONFIRMATION gate (>= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, >= 55% of videos winning, CI90 lower bound > 0). One LB probe only after that.
expected_gain: Gate-aware tail recovery: about 0 (+0.000..+0.0005). The measured learnable share of the tail is about 5% net (43/798 nodes), i.e. about 90 of 1,907 FN x 7.5e-6, or +0.0007 at best before crossed-out losses in the 4-7 zone. Plain 199-video de-quantiser retrain over the port: +0.000..+0.002 (a guess, since the quantisation ceiling is shared with the public head, which already takes most of it). The +0.002..+0.006 claimed in the hypothesis is not supported.
